creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-16, the second sighting after GitHub issue #1 part 2 (2026-10-07, 2817 bytes unread). Two Codex 0.162.1 panes on the devenv, side by side in one tab, went stuck one second apart (19:16:14 and 19:16:15 UTC) after a trackpad scroll over each: the first 2.9 KB left in each terminal was about 220 identical `ESC[<64;40;50M` (wheel up, one cell), and the copy pane's began mid-report, so Codex stopped reading partway through the burst. Each Codex sat at 0% CPU with every thread parked, scrolled back in its transcript (`Back to bottom`), and kept running turns: copy finished one at 19:16:29 while stuck. SIGWINCH and an emptied input queue did not get it reading again; only ending it and `codex resume <id>` did. The first burst is saved on the devenv at ~/inbox/stuck-review.bin and stuck-copy.bin.

The freeze is Codex's, but Muster triggers it. Next steps: reproduce with a recorded burst against a bare Codex in a PTY, record it under corpus/ and docs/observations/codex-0.162.1.md, and report it upstream. Then decide whether the daemon should coalesce wheel reports for a pane: one flick became hundreds of one-row reports at the same cell, where Ghostty's own scrollCallback sends the same, so coalescing would be a departure from Ghostty and needs its reason written down.
title: Codex 0.162.1 stops reading its input after a burst of wheel reports
